newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to enact bill for defector influx from North.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to enact bill for defector influx from North.

text.p: South Korean government and ruling party officials on Wednesday agreed to enact a bill to handle a possible mass influx of defectors from North Korea, a ruling party spokesman said.

The legislation would lay down how to integrate North Koreans fleeing the communist state into South Korean society and provide programmes to assist them, said spokesman Kim Chung-geun of the ruling New Korea Party.
"The agreement was reached in the meeting today led by Deputy Prime Minister Kwon O-kie, leading members of parliament and top policymakers," Kim told Reuters.
The bill, to be put forward in parliament within the next two months, also calls for construction of refugee centres in the suburbs of Seoul, he said.
Under the bill, civil servants and soldiers fleeing the North would be offered equivalent ranks and positions in the South.
Seoul would also offer special treatment in education, tax, housing, finance and medical care, Kim said.
Hijackers, murderers and those who committed serious non-political crimes in North Korea would not benefit from the legislation, he said.
A spokesman for the Unification Ministry confirmed the agreement in Wednesday's meeting and said:
"The move is part of government efforts to be prepared for all contingencies."
South and North Korea have remained technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended with a truce.
Arrivals of defectors in the South increased recently following chronic food shortages in the North.
About 600 North Korean defectors now live in the South.
